title: Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases: Estate and Successor Handbook, Non-Borrowing Spouse Deferral
content:
**Which cases can be deferred.** Under Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases, only a death case can be deferred, following the plan's deferral setting, and only on a HECM loan.

**Spouse requirement.** A death case is deferred instead of called due only when all of the following hold:

- the loan names a non-borrowing spouse whose profile is an eligible non-borrowing spouse;
- that spouse still occupies the home;
- that spouse has established a legal right to remain within the HECM deferral window.

The non-borrowing spouse named on the HECM loan and that spouse's profile are read from Cedarline's records for that loan.

**While deferred.** The case stays open without a call due.

**End of deferral.** The deferral ends on any of the plan's deferral end events. The case is then called due on the day the ending event is documented.

**Who cannot defer.** An ineligible non-borrowing spouse, or a spouse who married the borrower after closing, never defers the case and may only resolve it like any successor.

## Truth table (death case on a HECM loan)

| Spouse named on the loan with an eligible non-borrowing spouse profile | Still occupies the home | Legal right to remain established within the window | Deferred instead of called due |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | yes | yes |
| yes | yes | no | no |
| yes | no | yes | no |
| no | any | any | no |

A death case on a Cedarline Summit loan is never deferred, and neither is a case under any other plan.
